title.narrative: Urban Water Supply and Sanitation (Sector) Project

description.narrative: ADB has supported the government in improving water supply and sanitation services in 70 of the 176 small towns in Nepal through three small towns projects introducing continuous water supply, meeting national quality standards, and providing universal household connections with subsidized connections and affordable supply for poor and vulnerable households.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Inclusive and sustainable access to water supply and sanitation services in project municipalities achieved

320,000 people (including all poor and vulnerable)* in project municipalities have access to 24/7 piped water supply at 100 liters per capita per day, meeting the national drinking water quality standards (2018 baseline: 0) (*Vulnerable people are defined as those suffering the effects of marginalization within or outside their community because of their ethnicity, gender, caste, religion, disability, health, education, or socioeconomic status. For the project, this specifically includes Dalit, disabled, disaster-affected, marginalized, and endangered indigenous groups that are politically, socially, or economically excluded) Achievement: 312000 Progress/Status: 24 water supply and sanitation subprojects (20 water supply, 2 storm water drainage/fecal sludge management, and 2 DEWATS & Sewerage packages) are under implementation with various level of progress.
Base year population from 20 WSS subproject is 337,910 and will benefit from 24/7 piped water supply at 100 liters per capita per day, meeting the national drinking water quality standards.
Around 312,000 population served from 19 completed projects with 100 lpcd (around HHs benefited 56,000). Data Source: National census; annual and quarterly progress reports by PMO and WUAs; periodic project surveys (including baseline and end-line surveys); and annual TDF report Target value: 320,000

64,000 people (including all poor and vulnerable) in project municipalities have access to improved sanitation facilities (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 65000 Progress/Status: 65,000 populations benefitted. Data Source: National census; annual and quarterly progress reports by PMO and WUAs; periodic project surveys (including baseline and end-line surveys); and annual TDF report Target value: 64,000

Average time per day spent by women on water collection reduced to zero in project coverage areas (2018 baseline: to be established)** (**Expected to be determined by the end of the first year of project implementation.) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: As all the water supply connections are supposed to be connected in the household premise, the water fetching time will essentially be reduced to zero. Data Source: National census; annual and quarterly progress reports by PMO and WUAs; periodic project surveys (including baseline and end-line surveys); and annual TDF report Baseline value: To be established

Water supply and sanitation facilities operate at full capacity and operation and maintenance costs recovery (2018 baseline: none exist) Achievement: 19 Progress/Status: The water supply packages are designed to fully recover the operation and maintenance costs. This can be assessed once the facilities are operational. Data Source: National census; annual and quarterly progress reports by PMO and WUAs; periodic project surveys (including baseline and end-line surveys); and annual TDF report Baseline value: None existing
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: 20 WUSCs of registered WUAs formed with at least 33% women members and at least one woman in a key post (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 39.89 Progress/Status: 20 WUSCs of registered 20 WUAs formed (out of 20 projects); 20 contracted WSS WUSCs have 39.89 % female members; 20 contracted subproject WUSCs have at least one female member in key position. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
Sample project surveys

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: At least 20 climate-resilient subprojects that integrate GESI for future investments prepared (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 19 Progress/Status: 19 Climate-Resilient subprojects selected. Seven subprojects have been included in UWSSP implementation. 4 subprojects unfeasible due to low willingness from WUA. Ten subproject's detail/FSR have been received for review. A second list of 24 towns have been approved from MoWS. 10 are under detail study. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
Sample project surveys

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: Business plans and tariff guidelines prepared for project WUAs and municipalities, assisted by the Institutional Support and Service Advisory Unit and TDF (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 8 Progress/Status: Water tariff guideline for TDF and Water Tariff Implementation Guideline for WUSC prepared by TDF. Business plan of 5 from 1st & 2nd phase & 20 from 3rd phase towns prepared. 10 from STWSSSP and 8 from UWSSP are under preparation (the draft is near completion for Charikot, Hupsekot, Liwang and Pragatinagar). Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
Sample project surveys

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: GESI inclusive WASH plans, including priority investments for 20 project municipalities, prepared and approved by the respective municipality (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 18 Progress/Status: WASH Plans for all project local bodies will be integrated with recently developed National WASH (N-WASH). Training on NWASH tool completed and data collection is ongoing. The data for remaining part of the municipalities will be collected by DWSSM and municipalities. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
Sample project surveys

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (ii) 16 sex segregated public toilets with adequate space for wash facilities and design friendly to differently abled people constructed, with septic tanks (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 15 Progress/Status: A total 16 proposed from 14 subprojects with 15 completed and 1 under construction. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (ii) 20 water treatment plants, with an estimated capacity of at least 0.6 million liters per day each, constructed (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 19 Progress/Status: Treatment plants designed for all the water supply subprojects are with>0.6 MLD capacity. 17 projects completed and in service with more than 0.6 MLD WTP. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (iii) 60,000 connections for households to piped water supply, with subsidized connections for 6,000 poor and vulnerable households (including 100% poor households headed by women) (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 60400 Progress/Status: 20 water supply systems are planned with base year household number as 62,504. So far, 53,522 HHs are connected; 5,254 subsidized connections from 20 contracted subprojects completed.
Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (iii) Two decentralized wastewater treatment plants constructed and operational (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Two contracts for Charikot and Bhojpur decentralized waste water management system are awarded and at various stages of implementation progress. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (iv) 30 kilometers of stormwater drainage constructed (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 40.28 Progress/Status: 2 storm water drainage contracts in Katahariya and Tikapur subprojects. Both packages are completed with 40.28 km of storm water drainage constructed from 2 packages. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (iv) Climate and disaster risks*** factored in design of subprojects, as necessary (2018 baseline: not applicable (***Climate and disaster risks include seismic events.) Achievement: 24 Progress/Status: Ongoing. Design of remaining subprojects are taking in consideration climate and disaster risks. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (v) Climate and disaster risks*** factored in design of subprojects, as necessary (2018 baseline: not applicable) (***Climate and disaster risks include seismic events.) Achievement: 24 Progress/Status: Design of remaining subprojects are taking in consideration climate and disaster risks. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: 1a. Water supply infrastructure established or rehabilitated in 20 subprojects in 19 municipalities: (i) 2,000 kilometers of water supply pipes installed or rehabilitated (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 2690 Progress/Status: 20 water supply contracts in 19 municipalities are awarded and are in various stages of implementation. As of 30 September 2025, a total of 2,690 km of pipes are installed or rehabilitated. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: 1b. Sanitation infrastructure improved in 21 project municipalities: (i) 2,500 toilets constructed through output-based aid for poor and vulnerable households (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 3280 Progress/Status: A total of 3,340 toilets are identified from 20 subprojects. Construction of 3,280 toilets have been completed and are in use. Construction is ongoing for the remaining toilets. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: At least 100 staff (33 of them women) of DWSSM, TDF, project WUSCs, and project municipalities reported stronger technical knowledge of smart utility and project management leadership (2018 baseline: to be established) Achievement: 198 Progress/Status: Leadership and GESI in WASH training conducted in all three regions with 105 participants (6 male & 99 female). 109 participants from Eastern, central & western regions, TDF, DWSSM, project municipalities participated in the SMART utility management training (41 Female; 68 Male).
Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
Sample project surveys Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: TBD Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: TBD Target year: 2026 Target value: 100 Actual value: 198

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: At least 100,000 people (at least 50% women) covered by awareness campaign on water conservation practices and sustainable hygiene behavior, and 80% report greater awareness (2018 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: 226133 Progress/Status: Awareness campaign participated by and reached to 113,077 (50%) females of total 226,133 participants through formal/informal campaigns. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
Sample project surveys Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: TBD Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: TBD Target year: 2026 Target value: 100000 Actual value: 226133
